clue.text: Start to harvest a crop, baling fine source of fodder

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of harvest is used
baling wraps hay into a bundle, so one piece is bundled up inside another

parts.note: a crop is a yield, the amount a field produces
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A farmer begins harvesting, baling up a good crop to feed livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baling' puts F inside YIELD, after H (the start of harvest) and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow grown for hay supplies the dried grass that animals eat in winter.

clue.text: Refrain, given a black mark

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: Someone holds back after being given a black mark against their name.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back from doing something, especially from voting.

clue.text: Dressing in sheep's clothing, one was fired

indicators.note: clothing covers what is inside, so the sheep word is wrapped round the dressing

parts.note: a flock is a group of sheep
lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds

explanation.surface: A wolf in sheep's clothing evokes disguise and deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls a wolf in sheep's clothing, so 'in' reads as part of that idiom; here it is only a link, and 'clothing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An old musket ignited by a spark from struck stone was a gun, something that was discharged.

clue.text: Island National Trust's kept intact

indicators.note: Trust's kept reads as the Trust is kept, held inside the island word

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, an island
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: An island property looked after by the National Trust remains undamaged.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that preserves historic buildings and land; read 'Trust's kept' as 'the Trust is kept'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged is complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Nominally in partnership

parts.note: nominally here means by name: a surname made of two family names joined by a hyphen pairs them up

explanation.surface: Two people are partners on paper only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nominally' seems to mean in name only, but it means as a name; a British hyphenated surname (Bowes-Lyon) is said to be two-barrelled like a shotgun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphenated surname joins two family names, like the two barrels of a shotgun side by side.

clue.text: Endlessly debate an event in The Field

indicators.note: without an end, the final letter of the word for debate is dropped

parts.note: to debate is to discuss

explanation.surface: Someone argues endlessly about something reported in The Field magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Field is a British country-sports magazine, but here it means athletics field events.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a heavy disc is one of the athletics field events, as opposed to track races.

clue.text: Flunkey perhaps lurks behind group of people

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow close behind them
a body is an organised group of people

explanation.surface: A servant creeps along behind a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge doing menial tasks for others is a servant, as a flunkey is.

clue.text: Against including typical man or French song ()

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Against including typical man or French song ()', has its count missing and 'or' does no job: CON round HANS gives the answer, but the text looks garbled and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Against including typical man or French song ()

clue.text: Light accompaniment for this appearing reasonable?

definitions.text: Light accompaniment for this appearing reasonable?

parts.words: Light accompaniment for this appearing reasonable?
parts.note: the phrase with light added after and means outward pleasantness and reasonableness, so light is this word's partner

explanation.surface: Something light goes along with seeming reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'all ___ and light' means being outwardly pleasant and reasonable; the clue names the word that 'light' accompanies.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pairing this quality with light describes someone being outwardly pleasant and agreeable.

clue.text: Help with part of chassis twisted

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mechanic lends a hand with a bent bit of car frame.
explanation.definitionFit: To help someone is to aid them.

clue.text: Type of deer about, and others you mentioned, on reflection

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Type of deer about, and others you mentioned, on reflection', gives UNG ULATE only if GNU is supplied, and no word then defines the answer: 'Type of deer' cannot be both GNU and the definition.
annotationWithheld.clue: Type of deer about, and others you mentioned, on reflection

clue.text: Symphony, for the audience, didn't fail the test

indicators.note: words meant for an audience are heard, so the phrase is to be said out loud

parts.note: passing a spoken examination is having passed an oral

explanation.surface: A student succeeds in an exam, with a symphony playing to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: PASSED ORAL said aloud sounds like the answer; Beethoven's Sixth Symphony bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Sixth Symphony is known by this name for its country scenes.

clue.text: Hound fool to put money on outsider?

indicators.note: outsider says the betting word goes on the outside of the fool

parts.note: to put money on something is to bet
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A gambler is foolish to back a long shot in a dog race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outsider' seems to be a long-shot runner, but it says BET goes outside ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged long-eared breed is a kind of hunting dog.

clue.text: Result of joining workers' cooperative

definitions.meaning: a joining together produces a combination or merger
employees acting together to bargain over pay form a trade organisation

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a combining of things and an association of workers.

clue.text: Furnish seating, and help tours otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A guide helps run tours in a different way, and also fits out chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad and cover chairs and sofas with fabric is to fit out seats.

clue.text: To live and die, on embracing the church, shows special devotion

indicators.note: embracing means holding round, so the word on wraps the living and dying words

parts.note: taken as written
to be is to exist or live
taken as written
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A believer pledges to live and die within the church, showing deep piety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is a link; the Church of England is the crossword's usual church.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutiful compliance with orders or rules is a form of devoted submission.

clue.text: Report sudden expansion

definitions.meaning: a report is the loud bang of a gun or blast
a rapid increase, as in a population boom

explanation.definitionFit: A blast is both a loud bang and a burst of rapid growth.

clue.text: Second shopping facility cook shows children?

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
to fry is to cook

explanation.surface: A second shopping centre puts on a cooking display for kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks children as only an example of unimportant people.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignificant people, like little ones, are of no account, like tiny fish.

clue.text: Journalist initiates a greater check on horses.

indicators.note: initiates means starts things off, so the journalist word comes first

parts.note: a hack is a journalist
more means greater

explanation.surface: A reporter launches a bigger inspection of racehorses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check on horses' looks like an inspection, but a check is a restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitless bridle restrains a horse, a check in the sense of a curb.

clue.text: Horse appears right after some training

indicators.note: after says the right-hand abbreviation follows the training word

parts.note: a course is a programme of training

explanation.surface: A horse turns up correct after a spell of training.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift horse, especially a warhorse, is a poetic word for a steed.

clue.text: One side of London is stimulating

definitions.meaning: the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football team
to spur is to stimulate or urge on

explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur is a London football club known by this nickname; 'side' means team.
explanation.definitionFit: The football nickname doubles as the verb meaning goads or urges on.

clue.text: Check numbers about to be significant

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to count is to matter or be significant

explanation.surface: Someone checks figures that are about to matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A second tally of votes verifies the totals.

clue.text: Two officers arresting copper? Very mysterious

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the officers grip the copper between them

parts.note: OC is the abbreviation for officer commanding
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Two officers arresting a policeman is a baffling situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, the expected catch for 'arresting', but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Supernatural, secret knowledge is beyond ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Companion to Hardy given literary award

definitions.meaning: Stan, the comic partner of Oliver Hardy
a wreath of bay leaves crowned poets, hence the poet's honour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests the novelist Thomas Hardy, but it is Oliver Hardy of the comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan of the comedy double act shares his name with the bay wreath that crowns poets.

clue.text: Trespass, and fish behind small enclosure

indicators.note: behind says the fish comes after the enclosure

parts.note: ENC is the abbreviation for enclosure
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler trespasses to fish behind a little fenced area.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude gradually on another's property or rights is to trespass.

clue.text: Sat back playing flute, pleasantly entertaining

indicators.note: back means the word Sat is read backwards
playing suggests something loose or in play, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A musician sat back playing the flute, which pleased the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SAT into TAS; 'playing' rearranges FLUTE into TEFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing good judgement and refinement makes something agreeable to people of discernment.

clue.text: One nearly gets what Manuel says -it's most unusual

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for one is dropped

parts.note: a unit is one
Manuel, the Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, keeps asking Que?

explanation.surface: A waiter's puzzled reply is a rare sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s British sitcom whose bewildered waiter Manuel answers Que?.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one of a kind means exceptionally rare.

clue.text: Artist going to bank? Not very often!

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
to bank on is to rely

explanation.surface: Does an artist go to the bank? Hardly ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom happening means occurring infrequently.

clue.text: Start 15 in school, in a year?

indicators.note: in says the school sits inside the year word

parts.note: a date such as 1066 can stand for a year, hence the question mark
Eton is the English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil starts something within a year at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is EXPLOSION, so the definition is 'start an explosion'; Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to cause a blast.
